title: Pick the one domino push that topples the red tile but spares the vase
instruction: Make the red domino fall by pushing just one tile, and keep the vase standing.
context: Before touching anything, a careful robot predicts knock-on effects, as when one box pushed in a warehouse topples a whole row. The obvious push on the first domino sets off both branches and drops the vase; only a push on the red branch past the split works.
setup: Wooden domino tiles (1.2 x 5 x 12 cm, 50 g) stand 6 cm apart on a green felt mat. Two trunk tiles 14 and 20 cm in front of the arm bases on their midline lead to a 19 cm wide splitter at 26 cm. Two straight branches, 7 cm left and right of the midline, run from 32 to 62 cm; the last right tile is red. A glass vase (4.4 cm wide, 22 cm tall, 50 g) stands 7 cm past the last left tile. A Rubik's cube and a marker lie on the desk.
scoring: 0 if the vase ever tilts more than 20 degrees. Otherwise 1.0 if the red tile has fallen (tilted more than 25 degrees), 0.5 if another tile of the red branch has fallen but the red one stands, and 0 if none has. Scored at the end of the trial. The red tile and the vase are out of the arms' reach.
reset_notes: Stand every tile and the vase back on their marks; the 6 cm spacing must be exact for the chain to run.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only; the vase is a solid cylinder, so a fall counts as a break. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2), so falling tiles do not slide apart and the chain runs as with real wooden dominoes on felt.
